title: BOS-847 — under --host the add-account flow stops resolving the agent CLI locally: codex is refused with the command that works, claude drops to pasting a token

scenes.title: Reach the provider chooser while boss is driving a daemon on another machine

waitFor.label: the session board is serving the remote daemon's sessions, so this run is genuinely in a --host context and not an empty local shell

steps.caption: Boss is driving a daemon on another machine; the board renders that machine's work.

waitFor.label: the accounts table header, so [a]dd is pressed on a settled list rather than a loading frame

steps.caption: Press [a] to start adding an account.
The native provider chooser opened — both providers are still offered up front.

scenes.title: Codex is refused before anything is spawned, and the refusal carries the command that does work

waitFor.label: the codex registration screen is on-screen, so what follows is read off the flow itself

steps.caption: The codex flow starts and immediately reports why it cannot run here.

expect.label: the refusal names the destination it is talking about — remote context evidence read off the flow, not inferred from the fixture
the remedy travels with the message: esc pops back to the accounts list, so the operator has to carry the working command away with them

a frame carrying the codex registration screen with no exec-lookup failure on it: nothing was resolved against this machine's PATH. The pinned string is the one os/exec itself emits — there is no shell in this path, so a shell's 'command not found' could never appear and pinning it would hold on pre-fix code too

steps.caption: BOS-847: codex registration runs a local subprocess, so under --host it is refused up front instead of failing at exec time.
Back on the accounts list, unchanged — a refused registration stores nothing.

scenes.title: Claude drops to its paste shape, explaining why the walkthrough is gone and where a token comes from

steps.caption: The provider chooser, with claude already under the cursor.

waitFor.label: the flow reached the paste prompt, which is only possible without spawning the local claude CLI

steps.caption: Claude registration skips the walkthrough and asks for a token instead.

expect.label: the claude registration screen, so the paste prompt below belongs to this flow
the explanatory line names the machine the credential will be stored on — remote context evidence read off the flow

expect.text: Run `claude setup-token` in a shell on deploy@build-box.invalid (or anywhere the claude CLI is signed in) and paste the token below
expect.label: the REMEDY clause is on screen, not just the first clause: a bare `claude setup-token` also occurs in the opening 'the walkthrough is unavailable' sentence, so it matched on precisely the clipped frame this expectation exists to rule out. Pinning the second clause can only pass on a frame that actually wrapped it into view

expect.text: ^(?![\s\S]*Run the claude setup-token walkthrough now\?)[\s\S]*Paste your Claude setup token
expect.label: a frame carrying the paste prompt and NOT the walkthrough confirm: a walkthrough that could only run the wrong machine's CLI is never offered

steps.caption: BOS-847: a Claude setup token is account-scoped, so the --host flow pastes one and stores it on the remote daemon.
